title.narrative: Strengthening systems for health and scaling up of interventions against Tuberculosis and Malaria - Sierra Leone (01-Jul-2018-30-Jun-2021)

description.narrative: Sierra Leone, Multicomponent, Ministry of Health (MOH)This program has the following goals: To reduce the burden of Tuberculosis in Sierra Leone in line with the National Strategic Plan and End TB Strategy. By 2020, reduce malaria morbidity and mortality by at least 40% compared with 2015. To build functional and resilient national and district systems for health that deliver safe, efficient and high quality health care services that are accessible, equitable and affordable for all Sierra Leoneans. The objectives of this program are: To increase Case Notification Rate (CNR) of TB cases (all forms) from 217 per 100000 population in 2016 to 285 cases per 100,000 population by 2021. To increase treatment success rate of TB new bacteriologically confirmed cases from 87% in 2016 to 90% in 2021. To enroll and treat 664 of diagnosed DR-TB patients on appropriate treatment by 2021. To test all TB diagnosed clients for HIV and increase the percentage of co-infected patients enrolled on ART/CPT from 79% in 2016 to 100% by December 2021. All suspected malaria cases should have access to confirmatory diagnosis. All malaria cases to receive effective treatment. Provide access to 100% of the population at risk with preventive measures by 2017. To protect at least 80% of pregnant women and children under one year with IPT3 by 2020. To provide knowledge to the population such that at least 80% practise malaria prevention and treatment measures by 2018. By 2020, at least 95% of health facilities report routinely on malaria programme performance. By 2020, maintain and strengthen capacity for program management, coordination and partnership to achieve malaria programme performance at all levels. To close the Human Resources for Health gap at the PHU, hospital and DHMT levels; To restore Essential (basic) health and sanitation services to pre-Ebola levels; To ensure that communities trust the health care system and access essential health services; To strengthen communities to effectively communicate and send health alerts; and To develop health system governance processes and standard operating procedures
